POP-00019.bio: Born 2009, Oakland native. Shortstop, Oakland Athletics. Inner-circle Hall of Famer: 92.1 career WAR, 3x MVP, 447 home runs, 2,398 hits. $33.8M contract. Final season in 2041. "Precision" is the word every reporter reaches for. Hal Richmond wrote his farewell essay alongside Keane and Dillon — three simultaneous endings. The dynasty generation. Anthony: "Kelley's contract expires after this season." Kelley is not leaving because he failed — he is leaving because he finished. First spring at-bat drew a sound from the Mesa crowd that Hal Richmond described as something between ovation and grief. Lives in Rockridge.

POP-00021.bio: Born 2010, Oakland native. Left fielder, Oakland Athletics. 2x MVP. $28.4M contract. Dynasty Five member. Returned from ACL rehabilitation — cleared for outfield play. Hal Richmond: "Davis is intensity." Vacated the DH role gracefully so Ernesto Quintero could step in. Farewell season alongside Kelley, Keane, and Dillon. Lives in Laurel. Sat courtside at Chase Center with the dynasty core. The kind of player whose physical presence in the outfield communicates something about what this franchise expects of itself.

POP-00022.bio: Born 2012, Oakland native. Center fielder, Oakland Athletics. $37.8M contract — highest-paid player on the roster. Lineup anchor. Not part of the farewell generation — Horn is the bridge between the dynasty era and what comes next. The player the next version of the team is built around. Lives in Temescal. Athletic, energetic, bright-toned — the kind of player who makes center field look like the position was designed for him.

POP-00025.bio: Born 2016, Oakland native. Starting pitcher, Oakland Athletics. $8.2M contract. Spring stats: 2.00 ERA, 8 IP, 11 strikeouts. Bullpen/rotation depth piece. Reliable arm in a staff transitioning from the Dillon era. Lives in Laurel.

POP-00031.bio: Traded to the NY Mets - Born 2012, Oakland native. Third baseman, Oakland Athletics. Contract year in 2041. 6.8 WAR — quietly excellent. Spring training: 2-for-3 in opener. P Slayer framed him against Aitken: "You can find a Martin Richards. You cannot find another Mark Aitken." Richards is the harder sell but absolutely deserves the money. The next version of this team needs a third baseman who posts that kind of WAR without requiring constant management. Lives in Fruitvale. $750K current salary — dramatically underpaid for production.
